zh.title: 美國航空班機因旅客鬧事轉降 乘客協助以膠帶將其束縛
zh.summary: 美國航空一架波音客機因旅客失控而轉降，鬧事者遭乘客合力以膠帶綑綁壓制。
body: 美國航空（American Airlines）618號班機於2026年9月3日從達拉斯／沃斯堡（DFW）飛往紐華克（EWR）途中，因頭等艙一名男性旅客失控鬧事並言語辱罵旁人，迫使這架波音（Boeing）737-800客機轉降至巴爾的摩／華盛頓機場（BWI）。
該男子涉嫌在機上毆打鄰座旅客，並咬傷一名協助壓制他的退休警官。旅客隨後利用機組人員提供的束帶與膠帶將其固定於座位。班機於當地時間22時15分平安降落，警方隨即登機將其逮捕。美航表示對暴力零容忍，班機在該旅客被帶離後已續飛紐華克。

en.title: American Airlines Flight Diverted to Baltimore After Passengers Duct-Tape Unruly Man to Seat
en.summary: An American Airlines flight diverted to Baltimore on September 3 after passengers restrained an unruly man.
body: On September 3, 2026, American Airlines Flight 618, a Boeing 737-800 flying from Dallas Fort Worth International Airport (DFW) to Newark Liberty International Airport (EWR), diverted to Baltimore/Washington International Thurgood Marshall Airport (BWI) due to an unruly first-class passenger.

The passenger became belligerent, shouted slurs, assaulted a neighbor, and bit a retired police officer who intervened. Assisted by flight attendants who provided flexible restraints and duct tape, passengers bound the man to his seat. A traveler sat on his lap for 15 minutes during descent. The flight landed safely at BWI at approximately 22:15 local time, where police arrested the suspect. The flight then proceeded to Newark.

zh.title: 希臘空軍F-4戰機於飛行展墜毀兩飛官殉職
zh.summary: 希臘空軍F-4戰機於航空展墜毀；兩名飛行員殉職；地面觀展民眾無人受傷
body: 希臘空軍一架F-4幽靈式（F-4 Phantom）戰鬥機於2026年9月5日在雅典附近的塔納格拉空軍基地（Tanagra Air Base）參加「雅典飛行週」（Athens Flying Week）航空展期間發生墜機事故，造成機上兩名飛行員殉職。該架雙座戰鬥機當時正在執行低空機動飛行，隨後於基地附近墜毀並引發火勢。
根據現場觀展民眾拍攝的影片顯示，該架戰鬥機在進行低空右轉彎時高度持續下降，隨後隱沒於樹林後方並撞擊地面爆出烈火。希臘空軍官員隨後證實，兩名飛行員的遺體已經尋獲。儘管當時現場有數千名民眾前往觀賞航空展，地面觀展民眾並未有人員受傷。
事故發生後，現場隨即展開大規模緊急救援行動。由於墜機引發的火勢蔓延至周邊植被，救援單位共派遣約85名消防人員、23輛消防車輛，以及11架消防飛機與直升機投入滅火工作。火災狀況初期曾一度阻礙搜救進度，主辦單位隨後指示觀眾撤離空軍基地，並宣布取消該週末剩餘的所有飛行表演行程。
希臘總理米佐塔基斯（Kyriakos Mitsotakis）於事故發生後向殉職飛行員家屬致上深切哀悼，表示全國上下皆感到無比悲痛，希臘空軍亦隨之宣布全國空軍舉哀三日。「雅典飛行週」為希臘年度國際航空盛事，匯集來自希臘及多國軍民用航空器，2026年展演原定於9月5日與6日舉行。
希臘空軍自1970年代起即開始操作美製F-4幽靈式戰鬥機。儘管該型戰鬥機在多數原操作國已相繼退役，希臘空軍目前仍持續維運經升級改進後的同型機隊。

en.title: Greek Air Force F-4 Phantom Crashes at Airshow Near Athens, Killing Both Pilots
en.summary: Greek Air Force F-4 Phantom crashed during an airshow near Athens; both pilots were killed.
body: A Hellenic Air Force F-4 Phantom fighter jet crashed during an airshow near Athens on September 5, 2026, resulting in the deaths of both pilots aboard the aircraft. The two-seat fighter jet crashed while performing a low-altitude maneuver during the Athens Flying Week event at Tanagra Air Base, situated approximately 40 miles north of the Greek capital.

Video footage recorded by spectators at the event showed the fighter aircraft making a low right turn shortly before it descended behind a tree line and struck the ground. The jet erupted into flames immediately following the impact. Officials from the Hellenic Air Force subsequently confirmed the recovery of both pilots' bodies from the crash site. No spectators were injured during the incident despite the presence of thousands of attendees.

The crash and subsequent fire prompted a large-scale emergency service response. Approximately 85 firefighters, 23 specialized emergency vehicles, and 11 firefighting aircraft and helicopters were dispatched as flames quickly spread into surrounding vegetation. Early recovery efforts were initially hindered by the intensity of the fire, leading organizers to instruct all spectators to evacuate Tanagra Air Base and formally cancel the remainder of the weekend's scheduled flying program.

Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis expressed his deep condolences to the families of the fallen pilots, stating that the sense of grief was widespread across the country. Following the fatal accident, the Hellenic Air Force officially declared a three-day period of mourning. Athens Flying Week is an annual international aviation showcase featuring diverse military and civilian aircraft from Greece and other participating nations.

The Hellenic Air Force has operated the United States-manufactured F-4 Phantom since the 1970s. While the iconic fighter type has been phased out and retired by most of its former operator nations worldwide, upgraded and modernized variants remain in active operational service with Greece.

zh.title: Archer展開Midnight空中計程車巡迴試飛
zh.summary: Archer啟動Midnight空中計程車巡迴試飛；首階段聚焦加州城際航線
body: 美國電動垂直起降飛行器製造商Archer Aviation宣佈啟動名為「No Roads」的巡迴飛行計畫，將其Midnight電動空中計程車的試飛範圍，從傳統機場區域擴展至連接城市間的跨城點對點航線。這項巡迴試飛計畫是在與美國聯邦航空管理局（FAA）協調下進行，旨在評估整體營運準備狀況，並為該公司預計於2028年洛杉磯奧運及帕運期間提供空中計程車服務進行前置測試。
該計畫的首階段試飛聚焦於北加州地區，預計連接包括蒙特雷、霍利斯特、聖馬丁、庫比蒂諾附近的聖荷西、奧克蘭以及舊金山等據點。Archer日前已完成過往單月超過70架次試飛，近期更成功執行Midnight飛行器在沙利納斯市立機場與蒙特雷地區機場之間的往返飛行，首度展示該機型在兩個獨立機場之間的城際航線營運能力。
Archer開發的Midnight是一款由一名機師駕駛、可搭載四名乘客的電動垂直起降飛行器，專為短程都市及區域接駁設計。該公司指出，Midnight採用的電動推進系統能實現零直接排放，且噪音水平遠低於傳統直升機。該計畫旨在模擬商業營運中的實際旅程，目標是將地面車程需要一小時以上的陸路交通，縮短至約10至20分鐘的空中飛行，同時測試地面充電設施與空域操作程序。
此外，本次巡迴試飛計畫亦與白宮的電動垂直起降整合試點計畫（eIPP）緊密串聯，Archer計畫將跨城測試進一步延伸至洛杉磯，隨後擴大至德克薩斯州與佛羅里達州。該公司先前已獲選為2028年洛杉磯奧運的官方空中計程車合作夥伴，並於近期與AEG集團達成合作協議，規劃在洛杉磯市中心LA LIVE開發專用垂直機場。

en.title: Archer Begins Midnight Air Taxi Flight Tour Across US Starting in Northern California
en.summary: Archer Aviation launches Midnight electric air taxi tour in California ahead of planned LA28 operations.
body: California-based Archer Aviation has launched its US-wide "No Roads" flight tour to expand testing of its Midnight electric air taxi beyond airport-based operations. The programme is designed to demonstrate point-to-point regional routes linking city pairs in coordination with the US Federal Aviation Administration. The testing aims to evaluate operational readiness ahead of Archer's planned commercial air taxi services during the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic and Paralympic Games.

The initial phase of the tour focuses on Northern California, with flight operations planned across key locations including Monterey, Hollister, San Martin, San Jose, Oakland, and San Francisco. The initiative follows more than 70 test flights completed in August, including a round-trip flight between Salinas Municipal Airport (SNS) and Monterey Regional Airport (MRY) that demonstrated the Midnight aircraft operating between two separate regional airports.

Archer's Midnight is a piloted, four-passenger eVTOL aircraft tailored for short urban and regional transit. Powered by an electric propulsion system designed for zero direct emissions and low noise levels compared to conventional helicopters, the aircraft is intended to replace road journeys taking an hour or longer with flights lasting approximately 10 to 20 minutes while validating supporting charging infrastructure and operational procedures.

The tour is integrated with Archer's participation in the White House's eVTOL Integration Pilot Program and serves as preparation for expanding tests to Los Angeles, Texas, and Florida. In addition to being selected as the official air taxi provider for LA28, Archer recently partnered with sports and entertainment group AEG to develop a dedicated vertiport at LA LIVE in downtown Los Angeles.

zh.title: Airlink取消約翰尼斯堡衝場 民航局審查低空飛行數據
zh.summary: Airlink取消約翰尼斯堡體育場衝場；南非民航局對開普敦低空飛行展開審查
body: 南非區域航空公司 Airlink 已取消原定於 2026 年 9 月 5 日在約翰尼斯堡 FNB 體育場上空進行的編隊衝場計畫。在此之前，南非民航局（SACAA）正針對該航空公司於 8 月 29 日在開普敦進行的低空飛行表演展開飛行數據審查。

該次在開普敦 DHL 體育場進行的表演涉及兩架巴西航空工業E195（ICAO機型代碼E195）區間客機。根據 Flightradar24 的追蹤數據，領航飛機當時在距離體育場屋頂最高處僅約 41 至 46 英尺（約 12.5 至 14 公尺）的高度飛過。南非民航局於 9 月 2 日證實，已開始進行合規性檢查，並取得了該飛機的飛行紀錄器數據。Airlink 則表示，取消約翰尼斯堡衝場的決定是出於不利的天氣預報，而非受到監管審查影響。

en.title: Airlink Cancels Johannesburg Flypast as Regulator Reviews Cape Town Flight Data
en.summary: Airlink cancelled its Johannesburg flypast as South Africa reviews its low altitude Cape Town flight data.
body: South African regional carrier Airlink has cancelled its planned formation flypast scheduled for 5 September 2026 over FNB Stadium in Johannesburg. The decision comes as the South African Civil Aviation Authority (SACAA) reviews flight data from the airline's controversial low-altitude flyover in Cape Town on 29 August.

The Cape Town event involved two Embraer E195 (ICAO type code E195) regional jets performing a formation flight over DHL Stadium. Flight-tracking data from Flightradar24 indicated the leading aircraft flew approximately 41 to 46 feet (12.5 to 14 meters) above the stadium's roof. On 2 September, SACAA confirmed it has initiated compliance checks and retrieved flight data recorder downloads from the aircraft. Airlink stated that the cancellation of the Johannesburg flyover was due to unfavorable weather forecasts rather than the regulatory investigation.
